newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - NEW YORK TIMES BUSINESS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW YORK TIMES BUSINESS - AUG 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* The IMF and a group of Asian nations led by Japan agreed to a $16 billion rescue of Thailand's financial system.
* Credit Suisse agreed to buy Winterthur Insurance WINZ.S.
* May Department Stores and Nordstrom reported robust second-quarter earnings.
* Chrysler won a $232 million package of government incentives to build a Toledo, Ohio, Jeep assembly plant.
* The FASB said it would adopt its proposed rules on accounting for derivative securities, despite criticism from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan.
* Quick & Reilly has put itself up for sale.
* The Environmental Protection Agency is pushing an emissions-profiles plan that would allow easy on-line acces to data about the polution given off by factories.
* The dollar rallied sharply from its selloff Friday.
* The AFL-CIO has come up with hip new ads to woo workers to the union.
* BMW is running ads that focus on safety and value in favor of "the ultimate driving machine".
* United Parcel Service and Teamster representatives met with Labor Secretary Alexis Herman.
* United Parcel Service of America Inc's Teamsters union says its main goal during the strike is to win part-time employees full-time jobs that pay well enough to live on.
* Union Pacific Corp said in an SEC filing that it received offers from third parties interested in buying Pennzoil assets if its hostile bid for Pennzoil is successful.
* Shoney's said it settled its differences with dissident shareholders.
* Reader's Digest CEO James Schadt resigned.
